# Fluvi Engineering Journal

Shared evidence journal for the Fluvi prompt-writer and coding agents. Read this file in full before every implementation attempt. Entries record physically tested application SHAs, observed behavior, evidence boundaries, failed loops, commit/source audits, and the next allowed investigation scope. `USER_MARK` log entries are annotations and are never runtime proof by themselves.

## 2026-09-12 — Mind annual heatmap feature contract on application source `0d1a6ad2efcfe84465f46184888f93cf24d245e4`

- New feature contract, not an implemented-defect diagnosis. Exact last physical application at that time remained `92222edd...`; `0d1a6ad2...` was not physically accepted.
- Mind + Year only; exactly twelve MonthCards visually arranged 3 columns × 4 rows; each month uses square day cells.
- Heatmap must represent the same current filter identity: income/expense direction, annual time/year scope, category OR partner focus, then amount-range slider refinement; no independent filter authority.
- Live amount slider must recolor during drag. Existing `previewMindAmountRange()` is the live authority; canonical Query commit remains `onChangeEnd` only.
- Annual normalization is global across non-empty filtered days. Empty days are neutral; no-data/min==max semantics require explicit tests/tokens.
- MonthCards scroll; slider footer is fixed outside the scroll viewport and compact. Shared Query Menu presentation must not regress.
- Current prepared ledger rows retain `bookedLocalEpochDay`; resident membership data means drag need not parse dates or hit Room/repository.
- Parent `DashboardCoreModeHost` owns a vertical drag recognizer; child annual scrolling required production-parent gesture-arena tests.
- Per-slider-tick prohibition: no full annual row scan, repository/Room work, index rebuild, date regrouping, canonical commit, or unbounded cache.

## 2026-09-13 — Mind annual heatmap design approval and realtime-performance hardening

- Prompt-writer design approval branch lineage: journal-only `4d24b3722aae6e0c4f5229e490112dd5c6a2e773`; underlying application source then `0d1a6ad2...`.
- Approved architecture: one Mind annual projection from prepared ledger data, one upstream identity, existing live amount-preview authority, scrollable 3×4 MonthCard region plus fixed compact footer, RED tests before implementation.
- Projection invariant: rebuild only when upstream non-amount identity changes (year/time, direction, category/partner, other source-verified refinements, data revision). After build, slider work must be independent of annual transaction count; per-day sorted contributions + prefix sums/binary bounds or source-proven equivalent are acceptable.
- Identity/liveness: generation/epoch safety; stale scheduled frame callbacks may never recolor a newer identity; replacement is atomic from the consumer's perspective.
- Slider terminal invariant: final finger value must not be lost when `onChangeEnd` races a pending coalesced frame; thumb, compact labels, heatmap and canonical range must converge exactly.
- Normalization: global annual min/max from non-empty filtered days; real empty days neutral; non-empty minimum remains visibly non-empty; no-data year all neutral; deterministic explicit token for `min == max`; amount sign semantics must follow current source.
- Layout/paint: structural `Column + Expanded(scroll) + fixed footer`, one vertical scroll owner, one slider hit-test owner, scoped rebuilds/repaints; no broad Stack reorder.
- Calendar correctness: exactly 12 MonthCards, correct month lengths, 365/366 years, Feb 29, local calendar identity, no fake interactive nonexistent dates, narrow-width month-label coverage.
- Mandatory performance gate: production-parent profile with large synthetic annual data, preview compute p50/p95/max, FrameTiming, rebuild/paint scope, allocation/GC if available; 16.67 ms frame interval requires meaningful headroom. Automated profile cannot declare physical acceptance.
- Forbidden: debounce/cooldown, release-only recolor, stale placeholders, dropped latest value, duplicate filter authority, per-tick persistence/source scans, or hiding jank by reducing correctness.

- PROVEN calendar/layout source cause at `c4dc...`: `mind_year_heatmap_viewport.dart` uses a 3-column GridView with fixed `childAspectRatio: .64`; MonthCards give the painter an `Expanded`/`SizedBox.expand()` region; painter maps sequential day index by `index ~/ 7` and `index % 7` with no weekday offset. Therefore day 1 always paints in column 0 and card height is disconnected from true calendar row count. Replacing `.64` with another magic ratio is rejected.
- Required calendar geometry: seven columns are Monday→Sunday. Compute leading slots from the first local calendar day; map real day `d` through `slotIndex = leadingSlots + (d - 1)`; derive row/column from that slot; derive `rowCount` from leading slots + month length. A Wednesday-start month has two leading SPACE-ONLY slots before day 1. Nonexistent leading/trailing slots render no square. A REAL day with zero matching rows is a visible gray/no-data square. A REAL day with matching rows is colored.
- Robust height contract: preserve the 3-column × 4-row annual composition while making height calendar/content-driven, not fixed-tall. A candidate is four visual annual rows of three cards whose height follows the maximum calendar rowCount among those three months plus title/padding, or an equivalent source-proven constraint solution. Avoid expensive intrinsic layout on the live path and avoid another magic aspect ratio.

Current source already resolves the heatmap seed through `base.partitionFor(direction).focusMembershipSeed`; `DashboardFocusMembershipSeed.select()` assumes its supplied seed is already direction-partition-specific. Therefore “direction filtering was omitted” is NOT proven. Trace: direction input → selected/canonical direction → heatmap identity → `partitionFor(direction)` seed identity → projection build/ready → frame schedule/publication/stale rejection → consumer → actual paint, and repair the first proven failing boundary.

Because the retained snapshot begins already zoomed at `viewportSpan=0.756`, this proves only that the captured two-pointer attempt did not show an accepted scale lifecycle; it does not prove that no earlier scale ever succeeded.
- **PROVEN cross-band pinch owner gap at f6d6da7:** the parent `MindDetailedSumChart` owns the shared normalized viewport and raw active-pointer count, but every `_MindDetailedSumYearBand` still owns its own child `GestureDetector.onScaleStart/onScaleUpdate/onScaleEnd`. Two fingers placed on different visible yearly bands therefore reach the parent pointer counter as two pointers while each child scale recognizer can see only its own pointer. This source topology directly explains why multi-year physical pinch is much harder than one-year pinch and is consistent with the fresh seq-4889 ownership-without-scale evidence. The repair target is one parent-wide scale recognizer over the whole detailed chart interaction surface, with the shared normalized viewport as its sole zoom writer; per-band painters remain consumers, not independent scale owners.
- **PROVEN pan-morphology root cause at f6d6da7:** each year band computes its Y-axis `maximum` from only the current visible LOD sample and paints every Y coordinate as `point.total / maximum`. Horizontal panning can therefore change the visible maximum and rescale every surviving point vertically, so the same underlying data visibly changes shape instead of translating/cropping. In addition, `MindDetailedSumLod.sample` derives bucket membership from `(epochMinute - window.startEpochMinute) / window.visibleMinuteCount`; panning at a constant zoom shifts bucket boundaries and can choose different first/last/min/max anchors in overlapping time. Both mechanisms are source-proven morphology drift.
- **Required morphology invariant:** at an unchanged zoom level, horizontal pan must not change the financial shape of the overlapping time interval. Use a stable per-year Y scale for the current admitted identity/range (not a visible-window maximum), and use pan-stable LOD/bucket boundaries anchored to absolute calendar/normalized-year coordinates for a given resolution. Panning may crop/translate; zoom-level changes may legitimately change resolution. No fake interpolation or financial rescaling is allowed.
- **PROVEN Year 4×3 size regression cause at f6d6da7:** the new Year direct-grid header reserves `headerHeight=30` and the 4×3 solver is called with `viewportHeight = constraints.maxHeight - headerHeight`. The solver then derives `fit.cellExtent` from that reduced height and passes it directly to every month group. Thus the title/3×4–4×3 selector is paid for by shrinking the 4×3 day cells inside the same fixed card envelope. This violates the prior product invariant that adding the selector must not reduce the approved 4×3 heatmap size.

## 2026-09-21 — Balance all-time semantics + Mind-parity Header history chart clarification

- New product clarification supersedes the earlier Balance “current-scope” temporal contract: the Balance Header amount must **always** be the all-time/Sum net, `sum(income) - sum(expense)`, and must not change when the Summary Pill moves between Sum/Year/Month/Day or rail children. The latest-transaction carousel card has the same temporal-independence contract: it always shows the newest transaction from the canonical all-time Balance data authority and must not change merely because Summary navigation selects another temporal scope. This clarification is specifically about Summary/time scope; do not silently discard the existing non-temporal Query/filter identity unless current product/source evidence separately requires that.
- **Current-source mismatch is PROVEN at application source `c39f625e753d063dc053a1371bff0b9f4bae0c83`:** `DashboardCoreController._onVisibleFramePublished()` calls `_publishBalancePresentationForVisibleFrame(frame)`. That method deliberately derives income/expense from the exact `frame.scope.timeScope`, hashes `frame.scope.key` into `presentationId`, computes `net = income.totalMinor - expense.totalMinor`, and chooses `latestTransaction` from those same two temporal frames. Therefore both Header net and latest card currently follow Summary/visible temporal selection, directly contradicting the clarified product contract.
- `DashboardBalancePresentation` is currently documented and shaped as a **current-scope** model and carries no historical series. ## 2026-09-23 — Compound Balance Header chart mode clarification

- User correction: **Compound mode is a fourth selectable mode of the existing Balance Header linechart only. It is NOT a carousel topic and NOT part of the large lower Balance content card.** Existing Header modes remain: `adaptiveSummary`, `allTime`, and `monthEndClosingExperimental`; Compound is added beside them.
- Compound is deliberately **Summary-dimension-dependent** and switches projection source/aggregation by the current Summary scope while the Header's large numeric balance remains unchanged under the existing all-time authority.
- **SUM / AllTime Summary scope:** Compound shows a continuous sequence of **calendar month-end Balance closing values across all available years**. Example semantic sequence: 2024 Jan close, 2024 Feb close, … 2025 Jan close, … through the latest truthful completed/available month. It does not draw transaction-level sawteeth in SUM.
- **YEAR Summary scope:** Compound shows the **month-end Balance closing values for the selected year only** (up to 12 monthly closing points, subject to truthful available data). It does not draw transaction-level sawteeth in YEAR.
- **MONTH Summary scope:** Compound switches to the **raw Balance evolution inside the selected month**, preserving the transaction-level sawtooth: a large upward jump when salary/large income arrives, followed by the declining staircase/curve as expenses accumulate. The intent is to show one enlarged monthly sawtooth rather than suppress it.
- Product rationale: YEAR and SUM should expose the underlying long-term trend without repeated salary spikes obscuring it; MONTH should preserve those spikes because, at that scale, the monthly cashflow shape itself is meaningful.
- Compound therefore differs from the current three Header modes: it is neither always raw all-time, nor always current-Summary raw, nor always month-end-only at every dimension. It **mixes closing-value trend projections for SUM/YEAR with raw in-period Balance for MONTH**.

## 2026-09-23 — Balance Closings and Momentum linked-card design

- User-approved product decision: add **two separate linked Balance topics/cards** to the existing upper-carousel → lower-detail architecture: **Zárások / Period Closings** and **Balance Momentum**. This is new feature design, not a defect/root-cause claim. Existing Cashflow, Latest transaction, Top category and Top partner topics remain product features and must not be silently repurposed.
- Current feature branch before this journal-only entry: `feature/balance-carousel-v1` at `4c35adf0af7131f7cf010543fb53978886c7b344` (journal-only). Current application source remains `2bd7c356502a3e7e8cd55bb5431d72118ac99508` (`feat(balance): link carousel details to summary scope`).
- Current Balance architecture at `2bd7c356...`: one shared `CenteredCarousel` with a stable controller/ScrollPosition owns upper-topic motion; local Balance state selects one `BalanceLinkedDetailTopic`; one immutable Core-owned `DashboardBalanceLinkedPresentation` is built from resident prepared directional membership and drives the lower card. The finite topics are Cashflow, Latest transaction, Top category, Top partner and one prototype. The new cards must extend this existing owner chain, not create a second carousel, Query owner, repository path or lower-card surface.
- **Closings semantic contract:** this is NOT cumulative account Balance and NOT another line chart. Each bucket is its own period result, `net = income - expense`, rendered around a centered zero axis: positive net above zero, negative net below. Summary hierarchy is fixed: **SUM → years; YEAR → months; MONTH → calendar days; DAY → exactly six Balance-local dayparts**. The visual grammar is discrete diverging bars/columns; no cumulative line/area. Zero/empty buckets stay truthful at zero. Incomplete current periods show only actual data; never forecast.
- **DAY Closings boundary:** Budget currently has a source-proven eight-bucket, three-hour `SpendingRhythmDayPart` catalogue. Do NOT alter that Budget contract. Balance's six dayparts are a local presentation/analytics taxonomy. Prefer deriving them from the existing local-time facts (or directly from resident `bookedLocalTimeMinutes`) without new storage or hot-path work; freeze the exact six-bucket boundaries in tests. A source-compatible default mapping is: 00:00–05:59, 06:00–08:59, 09:00–11:59, 12:00–17:59, 18:00–20:59, 21:00–23:59. This mapping is an implementation default unless CURRENT source already contains a canonical six-part Balance taxonomy.
- **Momentum semantic contract:** Momentum must answer “is my net financial pace improving or worsening?”, not repeat Closings or the existing Balance Header line history. Moving average / comparable-window averaging is the calculation engine only; **do not render a moving-average line chart**.
- Momentum math: `currentNetPace = average net result over current/comparable window`; `previousNetPace = average net result over the immediately previous comparable window`; `momentum = currentNetPace - previousNetPace`. Keep current pace and momentum as separate dimensions: positive momentum does not mean the current net pace is positive.
- User-approved Momentum windows: **SUM = current year-to-date vs previous year over the same elapsed calendar span; YEAR = current month-to-date vs previous month over the same elapsed-day span; MONTH = rolling last 7 days vs the immediately preceding 7 days; DAY = selected/current day from 00:00 to the logical as-of time vs the previous calendar day from 00:00 to the same logical time. DAY must not use dayparts for Momentum.** For a fully historical selected scope, anchor comparison to that scope's truthful end rather than device wall-clock time; use the app's logical/as-of authority.
- **Momentum visual contract:** large lower card is a **2D four-quadrant Momentum Map**, not a line chart. X axis = current net pace (`deficit ← 0 → surplus`). Y axis = momentum (`worsening ← 0 → improving`). Quadrants: negative current + positive momentum = **Kilábalás**; positive current + positive momentum = **Erősödő többlet**; negative current + negative momentum = **Mélyülő deficit**; positive current + negative momentum = **Gyengülő többlet**. Exact-zero boundaries require explicit stable/break-even semantics, not arbitrary quadrant assignment. Compact metrics show previous pace, current pace and signed momentum. Insufficient comparison history is an explicit unavailable state.
- These cards are intentionally Balance-specific. Budget already owns daily spending-vs-limit pace/average semantics, so Closings/Momentum must stay net-flow/Balancing analytics and must not reintroduce average-spend or outlier analysis here.
- Upper-carousel integration intent: add compact previews for both new topics from the SAME immutable linked payload as the lower card. Do not perform independent calculations in the small-card renderer. The current prototype slot may become one real topic; adding the second topic may expand the finite logical topic list. Preserve the one shared carousel controller/ScrollPosition/physics and update tests rather than creating a second carousel.
- Data/performance invariant: reuse resident prepared Income + Expense membership already admitted by Core. Carousel selection is presentation-only and must perform zero repository/Room/index/scene work. Calculate bounded Closings/Momentum DTOs once per exact prepared identity + Summary scope/as-of identity and render them without rescanning source rows in build/paint.

## 2026-09-23 — Balance Cashflow Stability design

- User-approved new Balance insight: **Cashflow stabilitás / Cashflow Stability**. Its purpose is to answer **how predictable the net cashflow is from period to period**, not whether the user is currently positive/negative and not whether the trend is improving/worsening.
- Semantic separation is fixed: **Momentum = direction/change of net pace**; **Stability = dispersion/variability of net results**. A series can have near-zero momentum while remaining highly unstable.
- The primary stability measure should NOT be an arbitrary 0–100 score. Use a real money-denominated robust dispersion metric. Preferred contract: for monthly net results `net_i = income_i - expense_i`, compute `medianNet = median(net_i)` and `typicalDeviation = median(abs(net_i - medianNet))` (MAD-style robust deviation). User-facing label can be **Tipikus cashflow-kilengés**, e.g. `±84 000 Ft / hó`; the UI does not need to expose the statistical term MAD.
- Large-card visual is **not a line chart**. Preferred visualization is a one-dimensional net-cashflow distribution band around a visible `0 Ft` break-even reference: individual monthly net results appear as points/marks; a central/typical band communicates the normal range; the median net is explicitly indicated. Narrow band = stable, wide band = volatile. Avoid duplicating Closings bars, Momentum quadrant map, Cashflow Income/Expense chart, or Header line history.
- Supporting compact metrics may include: **Medián nettó**, **Tipikus sáv**, and **Szélsőséges hónapok**. Any extreme-period classification must be derived from the same robust distribution contract, not copied from Budget/outlier spending logic.
- Approved context mapping is **monthly-base stability at every Summary level**, rather than forcing noisy daily/daypart stability: **SUM → all complete months across all available history; YEAR → the selected year's calendar months; MONTH → the trailing 12-month window ending with the selected month; DAY → same trailing 12-month window ending with the selected day's containing month.**
- For the YEAR scope, only truthful represented months should contribute; current/incomplete month handling must be explicit and tested rather than silently mixing partial and complete periods. For trailing-12 contexts, the selected month anchors the window chronologically across year boundaries.
- Stability remains a Balance-specific net-flow insight and must use Income + Expense together. It must not reuse Budget's daily-spend average/limit semantics.
- No implementation prompt is requested by this feedback. Prompt-writer action: journal only, build-trigger-free `[skip ci]`; no application source, tests, workflow, graph, milestone or build configuration changed.

## 2026-09-23 — Ghost transaction semantics correction: lifecycle vs persistent provenance

- User correction: a Fluvi **Ghost transaction is not merely a conditional forecast item**. It has two distinct concepts that must not be conflated:
  1. **lifecycle state** — before its trigger fires it is a pending Ghost definition/event and is not yet a real ledger transaction;
  2. **persistent provenance flag** — after the trigger fires, it materializes into a real ledger transaction, but the Ghost-origin flag/badge remains permanently attached to that real transaction.
- Consequence for analytics: materialized Ghost-origin transactions are valid real transactions and may be included in financial totals. However, behavioral analytics may need to **exclude** them because large mandatory/fixed expenses can distort discretionary-spending behavior. Example product distinction: 100k restaurant spend is behaviorally different from 100k mandatory gas/utility/rent spend even though both are real Expense transactions.
- The analytics filtering problem is therefore **not the same as pending-vs-actual forecast state**. Recommended future Balance data lens is over **materialized real transactions by Ghost provenance**:
  - **All actual / With Ghost** = all real transactions, including triggered Ghost-origin rows;
  - **Without Ghost** = only real non-Ghost-origin transactions;
  - **Only Ghost** = only materialized real Ghost-origin transactions.
  Pending untriggered Ghost definitions must NOT silently enter historical actual analytics under any of these three modes.
- Pending Ghosts remain useful in a dedicated Ghost card for lifecycle/obligation visibility and may later feed an explicitly labelled forecast/scenario layer, but forecast inclusion is a separate semantic mode from the provenance filter above.
- Strong product rationale: one global/shared Ghost provenance lens is preferable to duplicating independent toggles on every analytics card, because mixed card-local filter states would make cross-card comparisons ambiguous. Card-specific compatibility can still be explicit where a metric should ignore or restrict Ghost filtering.
- Dedicated Ghost card remains useful even with the global provenance lens because it answers a different question: pending definitions, recently triggered/materialized Ghosts, lifecycle state, amount at risk/expected, and individual selection. The card may show both pending and already-materialized Ghost-origin items with clearly different states.
- Future data model requirement: keep **pending lifecycle state** and **persistent Ghost provenance** as separate fields/authorities. Do not model Ghost as a single transient boolean that disappears on trigger. A real materialized Ghost transaction must remain distinguishable from an ordinary real transaction.
- Current repository search on application source lineage found no existing `ghost`, pending-transaction, fixed-expense, recurring-expense, or triggered-transaction implementation. Therefore this is a forward product/data-model contract, not a current-source behavior claim.
- Prompt-writer action for this feedback: journal only, build-trigger-free `[skip ci]`; no application source, tests, workflow, graph, milestone or build configuration changed.

### Ghost semantic contract

- Ghost has **two separate authorities**:
  1. lifecycle: a pending Ghost definition/event is not yet a real ledger transaction;
  2. persistent provenance: once its trigger fires it materializes into a real ledger transaction and permanently retains Ghost origin/badge metadata.
- A materialized Ghost-origin transaction is financially real and belongs in actual totals, but behavioral analytics may later exclude it because mandatory/fixed spending (rent, utilities, etc.) must remain distinguishable from discretionary behavior.
- Future global analytics lens remains conceptually separate from this card: **All actual / With Ghost**, **Without Ghost**, **Only Ghost** apply to materialized real transactions by persistent Ghost provenance. Pending Ghost definitions do not enter actual historical analytics. This shared lens is future scope, not part of the immediate placeholder implementation.
- Dedicated Ghost card responsibility: lifecycle/obligation/entity inspection, not generic Ghost-only analytics.
- Approved future compact Ghost preview concept: **Fix terhek** with Ghost badge; hero prioritizes pending/materialized amount over count, with compact count/next-trigger context.
- Approved future large Ghost card: clearly separates **materialized/activated real Ghost-origin transactions** from **pending untriggered Ghost definitions**. Preferred metrics are **Aktiválódott/materializált amount**, **Pending amount**, and explicitly forecast-labelled **Várható fix teher**. A projected amount must never masquerade as actual Balance.
- Preferred future Month/Day main composition is a **Ghost timeline/list**. Materialized rows use solid real-transaction treatment while retaining the Ghost badge; pending rows use ghosted/transparent/dashed treatment. Tap opens local detail only.
- Future item detail distinguishes definition vs occurrence/materialized transaction and may show name, amount, lifecycle state, trigger, next trigger, last activation, and historical materialized Ghost-origin total.
- Approved future Summary behavior: **SUM → commitments/definitions overview + all-history materialized Ghost context + current pending obligations; YEAR → monthly fixed-burden overview; MONTH → strongest Ghost timeline/list; DAY → selected-day Ghost items with clean no-item state and optionally next upcoming Ghost.**
- Optional future secondary metric: **Fix teher aránya** relative to truthful Income. It is secondary and never replaces actual Balance.

### Forecast semantic contract

- Forecast answers: **“Given actual financial state, known future obligations, and robust non-Ghost spending behavior, where am I likely to close?”**
- Forecast must distinguish three provenance classes visually and mathematically:
  - **Actual / fact** — already materialized ledger reality;
  - **Known future / committed** — pending Ghost obligations (and source-proven known future Income if such authority later exists);
  - **Estimated future** — statistical non-Ghost behavior forecast.
- Pending Ghost obligations and behavior forecast must never be merged into one anonymous “expected expense” number.
- Historical materialized `ghostOrigin=true` expenses are excluded from the **behavior baseline** so mandatory fixed costs do not train the discretionary-spending estimate; pending Ghost obligations are then added separately. This prevents double counting.
- Approved first forecast model for MONTH/DAY behavior: **remaining-behavior forecast = robust median of the previous six complete months' non-Ghost spending over the same remaining-calendar-span length**. Example: with 7 days left in the selected/current month, take the final 7 days from each of the six previous complete months, exclude Ghost-origin materialized rows, compute each month's spend, then use the median. Do not use a simple mean and do not use ML in v1.
- Category-level decomposition may later explain the aggregate estimate, but sparse categories must not create fake precision; the aggregate robust baseline remains authoritative unless a source-proven category model is explicitly added later.
- Forecast uncertainty must be a **truthful typical range** derived from the historical remainder sample/robust dispersion; do not display arbitrary confidence percentages.
- Forecast large card is approved as **two pages**:
  1. **Forecast Bridge / Zárás** — “Where will I close?” with current actual state, known future Income if available, pending Ghost burden, estimated non-Ghost spending, projected closing amount, and typical range;
  2. **Forward Timeline / Kilátás** — “Why?” with known dated future events as concrete items and estimated behavior as a band/aggregate, never fake future transactions.
- Use subtle page dots/local page selection rather than adding another global segmented controller. Any page interaction stays local to the lower card and must not compete with Header/global horizontal mode navigation or the upper carousel.
- Approved Forecast horizons:
  - **SUM → rolling next 12 months**, not “all-time end”;
  - **YEAR → current year end**;
  - **MONTH → current month end**;
  - **DAY → same containing month end, starting from the selected/current day**, not end-of-day as the hero horizon.
- Page-2 granularity:
  - SUM → months;
  - YEAR → remaining months;
  - MONTH → remaining days;
  - DAY → selected day through month end, daily.
- Historical selected periods must **not** receive fake hindsight forecasts. V1 should expose an explicit unavailable state such as “Forecast csak az aktuális időszakra érhető el.” Historical backtesting is a separate future feature.
- Forecast may expose two conceptually distinct results when the data engine exists:
  - **Ismert terhek után** = actual state adjusted only by source-proven known future items;
  - **Várható zárás** = known future result plus estimated non-Ghost behavior.
  They must not be collapsed into one undocumented number.

### Immediate implementation boundary

- Because neither Ghost lifecycle/provenance storage nor pending-Ghost authority exists in current source, **do not add Room/schema/native/repository/domain trigger machinery in this task**.
- Do not fabricate fake financial numbers, hard-coded example transactions, or treat all current transactions as non-Ghost merely to make Forecast appear functional.

## 2026-09-23 — Balance Header history line visual smoothness feedback

- **User physical feedback:** on the current Android build the Balance Header history line is visually too jagged/noisy, especially where many transaction samples are compressed into the all-time 346×60 px plot. The user asks for a smoother visual line.
- **Current application source:** physical branch head is journal-only `b9775dd3`; the latest application source beneath it remains `65f33a4e388f6f796b77f31a5360e8f2f82a6f01` (`feat(header): add per-mode palettes and foreground`). The Balance history chart was introduced by `7ba0a989290e5a91169d409cb27e91d57baabd6f`; later presentation controls landed in `849fdef38218adf985f8f8584dc0365baf25e0cf` and foreground palette plumbing in `65f33a4e...`.
- **PROVEN painter behavior:** `DashboardHeaderTrendPainter` already uses anti-aliased round-cap/round-join stroke and midpoint quadratic Bézier segments, so the issue is not a missing `isAntiAlias` flag or a raw `lineTo` polyline. The shared plot is only 346 px wide and 60 px high.
- **PROVEN data density:** `DashboardBalanceHistoryProjection.build()` deliberately emits one exact cumulative sample per admitted transaction, retaining same-day income/expense reversals and extrema. In `BalanceHeaderChartMode.allTime`, the full raw transaction series is projected over the entire all-time X domain with no display-resolution decimation. Therefore multiple real samples can occupy the same/sub-pixel X span and create dense oscillation/teeth even though the path uses quadratic curves.
- **Existing alternate projection:** `monthEndClosingExperimental` already provides truthful month-close samples, and `compound` uses month-end closes for long Sum/Year views while retaining transaction-level detail for Month/Day. These are semantic projections, not merely cosmetic smoothing.
- **Diagnosis:** increasing Bézier curvature alone would not address the dominant all-time density problem and risks overshoot/false extrema. ## 2026-10-04 — Physical Balance Header glass feedback and renderer-layer audit

- **Authoritative current code line:** remote `feature/balance-wave-defaults` is at docs-only `9014df3dc3fc0586e53c25184c68cf59bca56e9f`; the latest application commit remains `d80bf76a0b08107d9ffb510d0f1f88ce530dc9af` (`feat(dashboard): add configurable Balance glass header`), preserving all application work through `271445da...`. - **Installed renderer set, source/lock verified:** baseline plus Flutter native `BackdropFilter + ImageFilterConfig.blur`, `glass_kit 4.0.2`, `glassmorphism 4.0.0`, `flutter_glass_ui_kit 1.0.5`, and `liquid_glass_widgets 1.8.1`. The exact versions are locked in `pubspec.lock`.
- **PROVEN current layer architecture:** `BalanceHeaderGlassBar` first paints one full-width `_BalanceGlassMaterial` for the track, then paints a second clipped `_BalanceGlassMaterial` over the left income-width region. For every blur-based backend, the second material therefore samples/composites after the already-rendered base glass rather than representing one physical sheet with a material modulation. The left income segment is a double-glass/double-frost region by construction.
- **PROVEN native white-overlay cause:** the Flutter-native adapter applies the backdrop blur and then independently paints a white material gradient (default start opacity `.20`, end `.05`) plus a second top-down white specular gradient (default `.22 -> 0`) and a white border. At the top of the base track those two white layers alone combine to roughly 37.6% effective white before considering the blurred backdrop; with independent income fill enabled, the same material family is painted again over the left segment, producing roughly 61% effective white at the top before border/shadow. This directly matches the supplied screenshot's milky full pill and denser white left 25% region.
- **PROVEN common-material homogenization:** all classic adapters are driven from the same app-owned default white tint/gradient/border model, so backend differences are visually dominated by identical white material styling. `glass_kit` receives white tint + white gradient; `glassmorphism` receives the same white background and border gradients; `flutter_glass_ui_kit` receives white frost color/opacity plus the same white background/border gradients. Switching those packages therefore does not constitute an honest package-native visual comparison.
- **PROVEN background-content limitation:** the Header physical shell behind the bar intentionally paints an opaque white base, then the animated Header visual material. The physical screenshot shows the bar sitting over a broad, already-smooth lavender/blue field with almost no high-frequency detail. A Gaussian `BackdropFilter` can only blur existing painted pixels; blurring an already smooth low-frequency field produces very little visible optical change. The white overlays then become the dominant cue, so the result reads as a translucent/faded white capsule, not a separate glass volume.
- **PROVEN no-op / misleading tuner controls:** the common tuner exposes `Glass tint opacity` and `Glass tint color` for Flutter native, but `_native()` never reads `material.tintOpacity` or `material.tintArgb`; changing those controls cannot affect the native renderer. Native `Backdrop grouping` is also instantiated inside each individual `_BalanceGlassMaterial`; each BackdropGroup contains only its own single filter, so enabling it does not establish one shared backdrop owner for track + income fill and cannot solve the double-filter architecture.
- **PROVEN blur sensitivity issue:** the supplied screenshot shows Flutter-native `Blur X 32.40` and `Blur Y 9.60`. On the current already-smooth Header field, such a large horizontal sigma removes rather than creates visible structure. Blur strength alone cannot create refraction/lens displacement; it only averages backdrop pixels.
- **Package capability boundary:** public package documentation confirms `glassmorphism` and `flutter_glass_ui_kit` are BackdropFilter/frosted-glass systems; `glass_kit` likewise demonstrates classic blur + translucent gradient glassmorphism. `liquid_glass_widgets` is the one installed backend with a shader/refraction-oriented pipeline and premium Impeller texture capture. ## 2026-10-05 — Budget secondary analysis and photographed FAB material delivered

- **Application:** `c85cbde62b6bec4ea8ec5f3999ce21db2b739d7f` adds the prepared Budget secondary-analysis feature; `829588c972a7064cf1c15048e9249958ea5a6d59` is the exact delivered application SHA after the test-only analyzer cleanup. Both are pushed to `3d-linechart`.
- **References and scope:** opened `/storage/emulated/0/spendee/source of truth/budgetall.png` at native 1312 × 1199. Its SUM/YEAR/MONTH/DAY composition drives the new Analysis semantic page within the existing Budget pager. The related interrupted FAB repair centralizes the inspected photographed `#06B6D4` primary and `#DDF9FC` highlight in `FluviFabReferenceMaterial`.
- **Architecture:** `DashboardBudgetSecondaryAnalysisProjector` converts the existing prepared snapshot into immutable `coreRevision + direction + targetHandle + scope` frames, placed in the bounded existing drawable-frame bank. The renderer only lays out and paints a matching atomic frame. The pager's established `PageController`, `ScrollPosition`, physics and idle rebase remain; modulo-three resolves Category → Partner → Analysis in both directions without a nested pager.
- **Data semantics:** SUM is the equal-weight average of eligible completed-month `actual / limit` values. YEAR uses `limit - actual`: a negative delta is red/upward from the central zero axis and a positive reserve is green/downward. Current-month forecast is `actualToDate / elapsedDays * daysInMonth`, while daily room is the non-negative remaining limit divided by remaining calendar days. DAY compares room before the selected day with room after its actual; terminal days avoid division by zero. All target identity enters the frame before title, chart and KPI publication, so category and aggregate data cannot be mixed inside a rendered frame.
- **Verification:** focused projector, card, visual-bank, pager and BNB suites pass 45 tests; scoped Flutter analysis reports no issues. The rendered production-card goldens cover one SUM semicircle, YEAR zero-axis bars, two MONTH semicircles and DAY Before → After blocks. Changed: a detached success still proves that the actual `HardwareBufferRenderer` allocation and slot-local shader initialized, and still emits `MATERIAL_ISOLATED_BACKEND_PREPARED`, but now immediately returns its unauthorised result via the existing fence-safe `dropReady` path. The direct instrumentation test now requires zero detached ready, in-flight and compositor-owned slots before first show.

### Proven failing boundary and repair

Chain: callbacks → queue/freshness/gate → reader/classifier → show decision → retained window → material controller/view/clock → attachment-owned draw callback → **service publication gate** → worker reducer/export.

`recordFirstRootDraw` / `recordFirstShaderDraw` previously emitted FIRST events only when `WakeTiming`'s cycle-first field was null. Nonterminal withdrawal retained WakeTiming, so a second attachment could really draw while its downstream FIRST events were suppressed. Window observations and material first-shader flags were already attachment-owned. Old diagnostics tests injected FIRST events directly; real-window tests ended at test lambdas, bypassing the defective service boundary.

Unit 1 extracted the existing condition into production `KeyguardDrawPublication`, used by the service, before changing behavior. Baseline RED: second genuinely owned attachment failed publication (**3 tests, 1 failure**). Corrected owner binds serviceSession/wake/attach, publishes ROOT and SHADER once per current attachment, rejects stale/duplicate/revoked callbacks, and retains independent earliest cycle fields. A second attachment removed before drawing produces no synthetic timestamps. Real-window CARD and ORB tests now route actual draw callbacks through this same production owner and original `KeyguardFirstDrawOwner.accepts` gate. They exercise real WindowManager/ViewRoot traversal and real frame commitment, not manual `onBootstrapFrameCommitted()` acknowledgement.

### Unit 2 contracts and bounds

Application commit: `d731827576802f3c35105e26237a436cfea1ebf9`.

- `KeyguardCardSettings.kt`: retained show and actual withdrawal episodes own canonical inspection timelines, independent of the rolling 16-request ledger. Delayed FINISHED records fill the same operation's cause. Snapshot copies detach these mutable records before formatting. Request provenance includes original trigger/callback/event/queue/start/finish/apply, request/apply visibility epoch, pending request, classification/markers, freshness/acquisition outcome and bounded slow-call evidence.
- `FluviKeyguardCardService.kt`: emits immutable callback/request timestamps and specific truncation evidence; preserves original finish time for aborted inspections. At actual withdrawal, after local hide/removal, captures a numeric attachment render summary and defers map conversion to the existing reduction worker. No diagnostic acknowledgement controls visibility or animation.
- `KeyguardWindowSnapshotReader.kt`: records `NODE_LIMIT`, `NULL_CHILD`, `CHILD_ACQUISITION_EXCEPTION`, `NODE_ACCESS_EXCEPTION` at existing incomplete branches; no extra traversal, node text or content-description extraction. Acquisition/freshness/classification behavior unchanged.
- `KeyguardDrawCadence.kt`, material view/controller and window accessor: bounded primitive counters for actual successful shader traversals, shader calls, phase advancement, first/last draw/phase, gap count/total/max and invalid ordering. Two shader calls during a transition count as one traversal. Clock callbacks remain a separate counter. Attachment reset excludes hidden idle time; no-draw episodes remain null/zero-count, not manufactured times. Snapshot only at withdrawal; no per-frame formatting, persistence, IPC, repository/query or scene preparation. Existing legacy field meanings remain unchanged.
- `KeyguardExportBudget.kt` and formatter: one 32KiB UTF-8 limit includes header, cold record, summaries, episode causes, omission metadata and footer. Complete compact episode blocks precede optional spine/raw lines. First + last three attempts retained; omitted critical records and incomplete attempts explicitly listed. No cap increase. Up to eight show episodes and nine hide records per retained attempt (eight withdrawals plus detached cleanup), rolling ledger bounded, semantic spine pruned with evicted operation ownership. Persistence uses the same bounded report. Recovery of older oversized reports explicitly marks line truncation and false completeness; frozen operational data remains immutable. Durability watermark still reflects successful writes, not freeze or clipboard success.
- Completeness checks now match each operation **and** attachment identity; a successful first episode cannot conceal a missing second add/remove boundary. `NO_DRAW_OBSERVED` explicitly does not prove no rendering. Native callback/Canvas observations are not Flutter FrameTiming or physical presentation.

### Implemented measurement contract and impact inventory

- `KeyguardDrawGapEvidence`: fixed three primitive slots per material View; exact previous successful shader-traversal end and current start/end, latest clock frame/entry/owned-work exit, prior callback entry, callbacks since last draw, CPU/configure/Canvas-call durations, current program and pixel extent. First/unpaired/coalesced observations, sampling breaks, rejected ownership and non-retained gap counts stay explicit. No output cannot become smoothness evidence. Initial draw has no invented callback. Non-live/bootstrap/static/fallback/pause time breaks pairing; hidden idle and another attachment/capture cannot form a live gap.
- `KeyguardMaterialClock` uses its existing callback/schedule sequence; primitive SAM avoids three new boxed timestamp arguments per callback. Controller still owns exactly one clock. View samples only successful actual hardware shader geometry; transition may submit previous+current programs, so exported `currentProgram` is not a claim that only one shader ran. No per-frame formatting, queueing, lock, persistence, file read, platform-state read or independent heartbeat.
- `KeyguardMainWorkEvidence`: service-owned Main-thread ring32, max3 overlapping own spans selected without sorting/all-slot object allocation. Kinds1=system fast-gate reads,2=inspection apply,3=diagnostic ingress. Records request/session/Linux thread ID, elapsed endpoints and whole-scope CPU. Nested/overlapping spans must NOT be summed. Ring completeness only concerns these scopes, not arbitrary MainLooper work. Unsupported CPU is explicit (-1 internally, NA/UNOBSERVED on export), never fabricated zero.
- `KeyguardCardWindow` passes attachment generation/provider to its retained controller. Actual View/controller detach both revoke measurement ownership; capture-token changes cannot reactivate a detached owner. Existing root/lifecycle/first-draw/frame-commit/bootstrap publication is unchanged. No new listener registration, View retention or renderer clock.

### Concrete next production repair — prescribed, not a new investigation assignment

Implement a narrowly scoped system-gate ownership refactor in the native service:

1. Separate system-state acquisition from the pure gate decision. Add an injectable production `KeyguardSystemStateReader` and one service-owned bounded `KeyguardSystemGateSampler` (names may follow local conventions). Recurring system reads run on a dedicated serial I/O lane, independent of the potentially blocked accessibility-tree lane; at most one active read plus one latest pending request. No per-frame polling, per-event job fan-out, main-thread wait/join, shared blocking lock, timed retry storm or privilege change.
2. Carry immutable request/result identity: serviceSession, wakeGeneration, visibilityEpoch, interactionEpoch, attachGeneration, monotonically ordered gateRequestId, capture/read times and reason. These values are identity, not a TTL permission cache. Do not hold AccessibilityNodeInfo/Event or View objects in this lane. Late Binder completion is rejected by identity; coroutine cancellation is not assumed to interrupt Binder.
3. Main retains exclusive authority over window, epochs, decision, retries and rendering. Direct SCREEN_OFF/USER_PRESENT, interrupt/disconnect/disable and privacy tightening invalidate pending positive publication and hide/redact immediately without waiting for a sampler/tree read. Privacy tightening must never attach a new root.
4. Replace recurring main remote calls in callback/retry/reconciliation/UNKNOWN/steady same-authority inspection paths with local identity checks plus bounded sampling. Preserve relevant event classification and immediate terminal branches. Already-visible same-permission inspection may maintain existing content, but cannot turn an old positive sample into permission for a new attach or new disclosure.
5. Keep the final fresh system-state guard at each real new attach or permission-increasing transition. Read one fresh snapshot at that commit boundary and feed both fast-exclusion/final-gate policy from it; remove duplicate same-boundary reads. This rare main boundary is deliberate to retain apply-time eligibility after a worker result waits in the main queue. Actual new financial-data publication keeps its existing current-state/privacy guard in this task.
6. A valid current negative surface result performs local withdrawal before retry-eligibility acquisition; detached UNKNOWN still preserves compatible pending work and does not churn epochs. Current system exclusion is a separate observation, not a stale surface payload's authority: a stale payload cannot suppress a fresh current exclusion, while an old-generation negative cannot detach a newer attachment. Never coalesce an already accepted terminal exclusion away behind a positive.
7. No diagnostic-only final candidate. No FPS cap, lower resolution, static bitmap, delayed hide, permissive UNKNOWN, permission cache TTL or weakened test assertion.

### Production ownership integration — 31a012ac

Application commit `31a012ac990154b932bf1cdf010526a9888f857d`, pushed and remote verified; candidate workflow `42902147702`. This contains an actual runtime refactor, not just observation changes.

Main still exclusively owns the retained overlay, visibility/interaction/attachment/wake identities, presentation, retry state, draw publication and material clock. A separate service-owned single-thread executor now performs recurring system acquisition, with exactly one active and one replaceable pending request. Main never joins the reader. Immutable requests contain every publication identity, gate request ID, causal event/callback/enqueue timestamps and unserved evaluation metadata. Coalescing preserves SCREEN_ON origin and freshness obligations without keeping Event/Node/View objects. Terminal invalidation revokes even a still-running read; disposal shuts down submission without claiming that an in-flight platform call was interrupted. Nonterminal authority changes reacquire once rather than relabelling an old answer.

`beginOrJoinWakeCycle`, event ingress, retries and stale-result reconciliation use this lane. Existing worker inspection signals maintain same-permission attachments; they cannot authorize a new attachment or greater disclosure. `applyInspection` retains one fresh Main ADMISSION snapshot for those transitions, rather than the former fast-gate read followed by repeated display/keyguard reads. Actual financial publication retains its separate fresh PUBLICATION guard, after cheap local ownership rejection. Reader failures and transitional display states cannot become positive authority or fabricated OFF. Existing tree reader, prefetch/cache policy and classifier exclusions remain unchanged.

`handleUnknownSurface` now withdraws before diagnostic/retry eligibility work. Timer eligibility is acquired off Main and the completed cause request is excluded from future-work detection. Hidden UNKNOWN still preserves compatible pending work/freshness. Privacy tightening redacts an attached root without acquiring remote eligibility, cannot attach a detached root, and revokes old financial publication first. SCREEN_OFF, USER_PRESENT, interrupt and opt-out still call the immediate terminal path; root invisibility/input withdrawal precede removal/cleanup. No window flags, z-order, geometry, clipping, touch/drag, shader/palette/quality, phase/clock, launcher, financial storage or Flutter/dashboard implementation changed.

### Changed contracts and retained ownership

`AndroidKeyguardSystemStateReader` owns the actual public platform getters; immutable `KeyguardSystemState` distinguishes unavailable/transitional state from definite OFF. `KeyguardSystemStateSampler` has one active worker call and one latest pending request, independent of the one-wide tree reader. Every request carries session/wake/visibility/interaction/attach identities, gate ID and causal timestamps. No live View, Event or node is retained. Main never joins or holds a lock behind the reader. Disposal revokes publication and submission; it does not pretend to cancel a blocked platform call.

```text
Main event/retry -> bounded system I/O lane -> Main identity check
tree inspection -> Main local stale check -> same-permission update
                                      -> ONE fresh admission read for attach/increase
direct terminal/privacy signal -> Main invalidate + hide/redact (no worker wait)
Main retained root -> existing controller -> existing single material clock
```

`FluviKeyguardCardService` routes recurring callbacks/retries/stale-payload exclusion checks to the sampler. Existing inspection-worker signals can maintain an already-authorized same-permission attachment, but cannot grant a new attachment or increased disclosure. One fresh Main ADMISSION snapshot remains for those transitions and is reused across final policies. A separate fresh Main PUBLICATION guard remains for actual new financial data, after cheap local stale rejection. Both can still block Main by design; they are counted separately from recurring acquisition. This is not a promise to remove all Main platform work.

Terminal SCREEN_OFF/USER_PRESENT/interrupt/opt-out invalidates before local invisibility and removal. Sampler revocation also protects an idempotent repeated terminal call. Privacy tightening redacts an attached root without system acquisition and cannot attach a detached root. Current visible UNKNOWN withdraws before retry eligibility work; hidden UNKNOWN preserves pending inspection/freshness. Completed cause requests are excluded from future-work suppression via `KeyguardCardInspectionQueue.hasCurrentWork`. Renewed work reacquires under new authority rather than reusing an old answer.

Production files: service, new reader/state/sampler, queue, signals/policy, and registry test accessor. Test files: sampler/admission unit suite, queue regression and real-service fixture; a local JVM harness compiles these actual production components. `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY`, flags, z-order, layout/paint/clipping bounds, tap/drag and saved positions remain unchanged. No parallel ViewRoot, animation clock, financial store or recurring polling loop was added.

### Confirmed cause, precise RED and correction

The failing owner was `FluviKeyguardCardService.applyInspection`: OCCLUDED used generic `hideImmediately` with its terminal default. That ended wake ownership and cleared pending inspection before `inspectionQueue.complete(active)` could advance. The reviewer req35/req36 sequence proves deletion of unserved intent, not misclassification or that req36 would necessarily return MAIN.

The baseline eb26d4d8 preserves21's lifecycle behavior and adds only an inert optional production-boundary seam plus actual-service regression. Run42920244421 failed at the exact intended assertion, “Recoverable occlusion erased the newer unserved inspection,” AFTER establishing current negative ownership and a pending newer event. The failure crossed actual classifier → Main apply → actual queue state, not a copied Boolean policy or setup timeout. Old tests did not cover a newer event arriving immediately before delivery of an older recoverable occlusion.

```text
old: current OCCLUDED → terminal hide → end wake / erase pending → no successor
new, hidden: current OCCLUDED → remain excluded → complete cause → pending starts
new, visible: revoke + local hide → copy pending intent to NEW authority/request
              → new acquisition → fresh MAIN + admission → one retained root
terminal: off/unlock/disable/interrupt/disconnect → invalidate + cancel recovery
```

Runtime commit7099f6c0 changes only service routing/intent ownership and the narrow awaiting diagnostic identity. `applyInspection` routes UNKNOWN/OCCLUDED through `handleRecoverableSurface`; `scheduleEvaluation` accepts an immutable reconciliation intent; `KeyguardCardInspectionRequest.reacquireAfterWithdrawal` assigns a new ID/enqueue/visibility/interaction/attach owner while preserving original event/callback/trigger/capture and outstanding freshness. It rejects another service/wake. Visible withdrawal never reuses the old acquired answer. Already-hidden exclusion does not hide again, end the wake or churn epochs. The active cause is never counted as future pending work. Finite16/32/64ms fallback and its budget are unchanged; repeated exclusion does not replenish them. Exhaustion waits for an event. Actual successful show retains the existing budget reset.

Terminal default/cancellation and fresh admission remain intact. No cached positive grants a new attachment or greater disclosure. Current privacy redaction and financial-publication guards remain. Credential/shade policy, foreign-window acceptance, cache/prefetch and incomplete-snapshot rejection were NOT altered. Diagnostics retain the OCCLUDED classification and do not inflate UNKNOWN counters.

SELECT s.id,s.ts,to_monotonic(s.ts) AS mono_ns,s.dur,s.depth,s.name
FROM slice s JOIN thread_track t ON s.track_id=t.id JOIN thread th USING(utid)
WHERE th.tid=2784 AND s.ts BETWEEN 456610000000 AND 456930000000 ORDER BY s.ts;

WITH w AS (SELECT ts,dur FROM slice WHERE id=267257)
SELECT state,SUM(MIN(t.ts+t.dur,w.ts+w.dur)-MAX(t.ts,w.ts))/1e6 AS ms
FROM thread_state t JOIN thread USING(utid),w
WHERE tid=2784 AND t.dur>0 AND t.ts<w.ts+w.dur AND t.ts+t.dur>w.ts
GROUP BY state;

### Source diagnosis and selected implementation contract

PROVEN structural coupling:
KeyguardCardMaterialController owns a Main Choreographer clock; its callback calls orb.frame/background.frame; frame invalidates the View; KeyguardHeaderMaterialView.onDraw records the shader into the same WindowManager ViewRoot rendering path. FluviKeyguardCardService application of negative/positive answers and KeyguardCardWindow visibility/window operations also require Main. A graphics wait in that ViewRoot therefore delays both frame production and service presentation control. Current trace executes this coupling; cheap draw CPU does not remove it.

UNPROVEN: that this one mechanism explains every Nothing stall, the303ms first traversal, the55ms callback-body outlier, all remote accessibility acquisition latency or delayed system event delivery. No claim that Android public APIs guarantee a particular phone frame rate. No phone performance improvement is asserted before implementation and physical validation.

The selected next task is a bounded implementation of render/control isolation for API34+ animated standalone ORB. It is an architectural repair of the demonstrated coupling and a falsifiable candidate for the phone symptom, not an open-ended diagnostics-only task or a promised complete cure. Its correctness and performance contracts must be RED/GREEN tested on the actual overlay before release.

Concrete design:
1. Keep the existing service, fresh admission, privacy, one WindowManager root, gestures and pending-work/epoch policies. CARD, <=API33, static/OFF, launcher widgets and dashboard keep their established routes.
2. For API34+ animated ORB, replace the active per-frame View invalidation path with one dedicated HandlerThread/Choreographer producer rendering the canonical AGSL through RenderNode + platform HardwareBufferRenderer into a fixed three-slot HardwareBuffer pool. No second concurrent animation clock/backend.
3. The worker owns mutable RuntimeShader/Paint/RenderNode and all render invocation/fence work. Main never waits for render completion, fences, worker joins or resource destruction. All HardwareBufferRenderer instances still share Android's RenderThread; this is control-path isolation, not a private GPU or guaranteed faster shader.
4. Publish GPU-ready buffers to a non-input child SurfaceControl parented to the EXISTING Fluvi overlay root using its AttachedSurfaceControl. Do not parent to SystemUI or replace the visibility authority/window type. BuildReparentTransaction has a nullable result; unavailable attachment stays hidden and event-recoverable.
5. Main alone creates/reparents/shows/hides child layers and authorizes an exact session/wake/visibility/attach/content/privacy lease. The worker may only update buffers on its leased layer; it never shows/reparents a layer. Each withdrawal/privacy invalidation retires that layer; never recycle its identity into a new authority epoch. A raced old setBuffer cannot make a hidden/unparented old layer visible.
6. Perform immediate child hide/reparent-null from Main before root removal/slow cleanup. Cancel current lease before async work. Do not queue hide behind rendering. Defer GPU object cleanup safely. Bound retired resources and replacements globally; do not allocate new pools/layers indefinitely during rapid wake/mode changes.
7. Use exact measured orb dimensions, RGBA8888 premultiplied transparency, existing circle/AA, canonical profile/phase/180ms semantic transition. Full-to-neutral changes revoke old presentation before new publication and never crossfade financial colours.
8. Do not send unsignaled producer fences into a compositor queue ahead of hide: readiness/fence checks are worker-side; release fences also govern safe reuse. Three slots with explicit FREE/RENDERING/READY/COMPOSITOR_OWNED/RETIRED states; one in-flight render and latest-only desired state, no catch-up queue. Clear transparent pixels every frame. Size and usage support checked without lowering visual fidelity.
9. Prepare this SAME bounded rendering backend offscreen while detached; preparation grants no visibility. A ready, current, authorized buffer need not wait for an unrelated bootstrap View commit. If not ready, preserve safe fallback and later automatic promotion; late results cannot revive retired authority. Preserve legacy bootstrap tests for the legacy backend.
10. Add backend-specific CPU-record/GPU-ready/buffer-submission evidence. Do not rename old CPU-draw counters as physical presentation, compare old/new incompatible timings, or turn UNOBSERVED into0.

Relevant official API contracts reviewed2026-11-11:
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/HardwareBufferRenderer
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/HardwareBufferRenderer.RenderRequest
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/HardwareBufferRenderer.RenderResult
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/SurfaceControl.Transaction
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/AttachedSurfaceControl
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/Choreographer

Platform HardwareBufferRenderer is API34, exposes obtainRenderRequest().draw(executor, callback), shares RenderThread, preserves existing buffer contents unless cleared, and does not close the caller's HardwareBuffer. SurfaceControl setBuffer requires COMPOSER_OVERLAY and GPU_SAMPLED_IMAGE usage; render targets also require GPU_COLOR_OUTPUT. Its release callback/fence controls reuse. These documented contracts justify the API design; they do not establish a phone root cause.

### Source-proven defects and reachable failure paths at 81c8d4b

1. Incorrect lower-level screenshot target:
   - The compositor test creates a separate TYPE_APPLICATION_PANEL through TestPanelWindowManager, but copyWindow calls PixelCopy.request(activity.window, ...).
   - PixelCopy of the Activity window targets that window's Surface, not a whole-display composite including a separately added panel. This assertion is not a valid oracle for the child attached to the panel.
   - The real-service fixture uses a compositor screenshot and therefore independently demonstrates a real visible-output failure. Fixing the false target must not be used to dismiss that failure.

2. Fixed-pool recovery can shrink to a self-stalling single slot:
   - KeyguardOrbBufferRenderer.Worker.retire changes owned slots to RETIRED but keeps FREE slots.
   - release, dropReady and stale render completion remove retired slots.
   - ensureResources returns true for a matching-size pool containing ANY non-retired slot; it never replenishes a partially depleted pool in that branch.
   - Reachable schedule: A compositor-owned, B rendering, C free -> retirement -> A/B safely finish and are removed -> only C remains -> C is published and becomes compositor-owned -> no free target exists for the replacement transaction that would release C. The existing guard keeps returning true without restoring capacity.
   - This is a source-demonstrable liveness defect. A deterministic production-state-machine test must reproduce it; the exact slot schedule causing the retained CI failures has not been proven.

3. Retirement destroys the ownership information required by disposal:
   - Controller disposal calls stop/onDetached/retire and renderer.dispose; renderer.dispose retires again.
   - Worker.retire collapses RENDERING, READY_FOR_MAIN and COMPOSITOR_OWNED into RETIRED.
   - Worker.dispose's awaitingRelease filter includes only the three pre-retirement states and excludes RETIRED. It can consequently close buffers still owned by GPU/handoff/compositor and end the callback owner early.
   - Retirement must be orthogonal to owner/fence state; repeated retire/dispose must be idempotent. An enum rename or another special-case filter is not a complete state-machine repair.

4. Fence and resize safety are incomplete:
   - Stale/error render completion and dropReady close the render-result fence and can free/remove a buffer without establishing that GPU use has finished.
   - ensureResources' resize protection covers COMPOSITOR_OWNED/RETIRED but does not independently protect RENDERING/READY_FOR_MAIN before closing the pool.
   - release waits indefinitely for a release fence on the sole worker Handler, blocking its own configure/retire/recovery processing.
   - A transaction-committed callback is not a buffer-release callback. The Android API requires waiting on a valid release fence before reuse. Never treat a timeout or discarded callback as permission to reuse or close an owned buffer.

5. The isolation and LIVE boundary remain incomplete:
   - Every onFrameReady posts to Main, and publishReady performs setBuffer and setVisibility(true) there. Steady-state publication remains dependent on the service Main queue.

## 2026-11-11 — submitted acquire-fence ownership correction (`84c30caf`)

- API35 run `42989373258` compiled the candidate and passed core/Flutter tests, but both the actual accessibility-overlay crop and the corrected panel crop remained static while isolated submissions advanced. Human APK was correctly skipped.
- The runtime source still closed the acquire fence after successful `SurfaceControl.Transaction.setBuffer`. Android's public `setBuffer` contract transfers a submitted acquire fence to SurfaceControl; it must remain valid while the compositor waits before display. The old close could invalidate that wait and is a concrete producer-to-compositor ownership violation.

## 2026-11-11 — AGSL specialization correction and zero-Portal program selection candidate

- The `uEffect` conclusion above was falsified by the exact packaged AGSL from run `43014053786`: the `dualTide` program declares `const float uEffect = 1.0`, not a uniform. The adapter deliberately replaces the canonical `uniform float uEffect;` with an effect-specific compile-time constant to keep the API-35 program within its size budget. Consequently `RuntimeShader.setFloatUniform("uEffect", …)` is invalid and the run failed before drawing with `COMPILE_OR_UNIFORM_FAILED`; it is removed.
- The real-service fixture marks its background Portal enabled but supplies `effectIndex=0`. Canonical `portalSample` returns zero for that sentinel, so this channel has no material, phase, palette, or pixel contribution even though it remains semantically enabled. `KeyguardMaterialProfile.requiresPortalProgram` now distinguishes that case from a materially active Portal channel. Artifact preparation, matching and isolated-ORB reconciliation choose the compact `plain` AGSL only when both enabled channels have the zero-effect sentinel; nonzero enabled Portal effects retain the `portal` AGSL.
- This preserves semantic `usesPortal` diagnostics, profile visual identity, phase clock, effect specialization, buffer ownership and all visibility/privacy authority. It does not make an active Portal disappear. The lower isolated-ORB instrumentation profile now uses an enabled nonzero Portal effect, so the API-35 lower gate will continue to exercise the full Portal program rather than making the compact selection a coverage escape.
- PASS — `git diff --check`; PASS — Ubuntu/proot `scripts/test-keyguard-system-gate-jvm.sh` (37 tests). Local targeted `:app:testDebugUnitTest --tests …KeyguardMaterialProfileTest` reached `:app:processDebugResources` but could not start the ARM/proot AAPT2 daemon (`aapt2-8.11.1-12782657-linux`) before Kotlin/test compilation; this is not counted as a test pass. The following scratch-only Python/NumPy evaluation was executed by the reviewer. SHA256 of the original script: `6c15a8bc3974ec8689b15ce0f326621cd54a21bfe08bf1e57f07f6037c2da4a4`. It must not replace Android correctness tests or be copied into production rendering.

```python
import numpy as np

# Reviewer-only numeric evaluation of the unchanged dualTide equations.
# This is not Android/GPU runtime evidence and is not production shader code.
F=np.float32
def fract(v): return v-np.floor(v)
def hash_(v,seed):
    c=np.floor(v)
    a=fract(c[...,[0,1,0]]*F(.1031)+F(seed)*F(.0173))
    d=np.sum(a*(a[...,[1,2,0]]+F(33.33)),axis=-1)
    a=a+d[...,None]
    return fract((a[...,0]+a[...,1])*a[...,2])
def noise(v,seed):
    c=np.floor(v); fr=fract(v); e=fr*fr*(F(3)-F(2)*fr)
    a=hash_(c,seed); b=hash_(c+np.array([1,0],dtype=F),seed)
    top=a+(b-a)*e[...,0]
    a=hash_(c+np.array([0,1],dtype=F),seed); b=hash_(c+F(1),seed)
    bot=a+(b-a)*e[...,0]
    return top+(bot-top)*e[...,1]
def fbm(v,seed):
    total=np.zeros(v.shape[:-1],dtype=F); amp=F(.58); norm=F(0); freq=F(1)
    for i in range(3):
        total += noise(v*freq,F(seed)+F(i)*F(17.3))*amp
        norm+=amp; freq*=F(1.93); amp*=F(.46)
    return total/norm
def evaluate(phase,settings=None):
    m=np.full(40,.2,dtype=F) if settings is None else np.array(settings,dtype=F)
    y,x=np.mgrid[0:168,0:168].astype(F)
    uv=np.stack([(x+F(.5))/F(168),(y+F(.5))/F(168)],axis=-1)
    p=F(.5)+(uv-F(.5))*max(F(.01),m[5]); phase=F(phase); pi=F(np.pi)
    ratio=m[2]+np.sin(phase*m[4]*pi*F(2))*m[3]; mt=phase*m[7]
    broad=(fbm(p*np.array([1.17,1.09],dtype=F)+np.array([mt*F(.07),-mt*F(.05)],dtype=F),31.7)-F(.5))*m[6]
    fine=(fbm(p*np.array([2.8,2.5],dtype=F)+np.array([-mt*F(.09),mt*F(.08)],dtype=F),67.3)-F(.5))*m[9]
    field=p[...,0]+ratio+broad*F(.20)+fine*F(.12)
    ap=phase*F(.52); bp=phase*F(.47)+m[23]*pi/F(180)
    ax=F(.5)-m[18]*F(.5)+np.sin(ap*F(.83))*m[15]+(F(.5)+F(.5)*np.sin(ap*F(.31)))*m[17]
    bx=F(.5)+m[18]*F(.5)-np.sin(bp*F(.79))*m[15]-(F(.5)+F(.5)*np.sin(bp*F(.29)))*m[17]
    ay=F(.5)+np.sin(ap*F(.61))*m[16]; by=F(.5)-np.sin(bp*F(.57))*m[16]
    def mass(cx,cy,rx,ry):
        d=(p-np.array([cx,cy],dtype=F))/np.maximum(np.array([rx,ry],dtype=F),F(.0001))
        return np.exp(-np.sum(d*d,axis=-1))
    am=mass(ax,ay,m[19],m[19]/max(F(.01),m[21])); bm=mass(bx,by,m[20],m[20]/max(F(.01),m[22]))
    warp=(fbm(p*m[26]+np.array([phase*m[27]*F(.11),-phase*m[27]*F(.09)],dtype=F),103.2)-F(.5))*m[25]
    field+=warp+(bm-am)*m[24]*F(.46)
    local=(am+bm-F(.7))*m[12]*F(.12)
    soft=max(F(.001),m[8]); t=np.clip((field-(F(.5)-soft))/max(F(.000001),F(2)*soft),0,1)
    mixture=t*t*(F(3)-F(2)*t); seam=F(4)*mixture*(F(1)-mixture)
    pulse=np.sin(phase*m[11]*pi*F(2))*m[10]
    light=np.clip((pulse+(broad+fine)*m[12]+local)*seam,-.25,.25)
    size=np.array([390,220],dtype=F); direction=np.array([.9271838546,.3746065934],dtype=F)
    length=np.sum(abs(direction)*size); start=size*F(.5)-direction*length*F(.5)
    base=np.clip(np.sum((uv*size-start)*direction,axis=-1)/length,0,1)
    coordinate=np.clip(base+(mixture-p[...,0])*np.clip(m[0],0,1)*F(4)*base*(F(1)-base),0,1)
    cols=np.array([[16,79,124],[98,199,220],[131,102,220]],dtype=F)/F(255)
    amt=np.where(coordinate<=F(.5),coordinate*F(2),(coordinate-F(.5))*F(2))
    rgb=np.where((coordinate<=F(.5))[...,None],cols[0]+(cols[1]-cols[0])*amt[...,None],cols[1]+(cols[2]-cols[1])*amt[...,None])
    rgb=np.clip(rgb*(F(1)+light[...,None]),0,1)
    mask=(x-F(83.5))**2+(y-F(83.5))**2<F(80)**2
    stats=dict(phase=float(phase),ratio=float(ratio),field_min=float(field[mask].min()),field_max=float(field[mask].max()),mixture_min=float(mixture[mask].min()),mixture_max=float(mixture[mask].max()),max_abs_light=float(abs(light[mask]).max()))
    return np.rint(rgb*F(255)).astype(int),mask,stats

if __name__=='__main__':
    phases=[1.196795,1.5234617,.97574466,1.8890779,.25,.35,3.75]
    images=[]
    for ph in phases:
        im,mask,stats=evaluate(ph);images.append(im);print(stats)
    for a,b in [(0,1),(2,3),(4,5),(4,6),(0,6)]:
        delta=abs(images[a]-images[b]).max(axis=-1)[mask]
        print('PAIR',phases[a],phases[b],dict(changed_ge7=int((delta>=7).sum()),sum_delta=int(delta.sum()),max_delta=int(delta.max())))
```

### New concrete diagnosis: numeric equality is incorrectly used as CAS identity

File at the reviewed SHA: `android/app/src/androidTest/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/KeyguardServiceOverlayInstrumentationTest.kt`, ProducerPixelProbe lines 379–431.

```kotlin
private val requestedPhase = AtomicReference<Float?>(null)
// awaitPhase:
requestedPhase.set(phase)
// onProduced:
val phase = requestedPhase.get() ?: return
// ... matching phase, fence wait, successful pixel copy ...
if (requestedPhase.compareAndSet(phase, null)) captured.set(sample)
```

- AtomicReference.compareAndSet compares object reference identity, not floating-point numeric equality. The non-null local Float is unboxed and boxed again at the CAS boundary; its expected reference is not the object stored by set(phase). Thus a correct phase and successful readback can be discarded, captured remains null, and awaitPhase emits a misleading 'producer did not reach requested phase' timeout.
- This is a source-level sufficient failure mechanism, reproduced independently. The current CI does not log every readback/CAS outcome, so the reviewer does not claim all intermediate Android callbacks have been traced.
- Strong corroboration from the actual CI compile log at 2026-11-11T19:28:38.6891933Z: `KeyguardServiceOverlayInstrumentationTest.kt:414:25 This call may have inconsistent results because 'AtomicReference' uses identity equality and 'Float?' does not have a consistent identity.`
- Reviewer ran the minimal equivalent Kotlin/JVM sequence below, first with Kotlin 2.2.0 and then **the project's exact Kotlin 2.2.20** (as declared in android/settings.gradle.kts), JRE 21.0.13. Both returned: `Float phase CAS success=0/100; request-token CAS success=100/100`. Kotlin 2.2.20 also emitted the same identity warning. This is an executed JVM reproducer, not Android instrumentation or a phone performance result.
- Official reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/24/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/atomic/AtomicReference.html#compareAndSet(V,V)

```kotlin
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference

fun main() {
    val requestedPhase = AtomicReference<Float?>(null)
    var legacySuccess = 0
    repeat(100) {
        requestedPhase.set(1.196795f)
        val phase = requestedPhase.get() ?: error("missing")
        check(kotlin.math.abs(1.196795f - phase) <= .0001f)
        if (requestedPhase.compareAndSet(phase, null)) legacySuccess++
    }
    data class Request(val id: Long, val phase: Float)
    val requested = AtomicReference<Request?>(null)
    var tokenSuccess = 0
    repeat(100) {
        requested.set(Request(it.toLong(), 1.196795f))
        val request = requested.get() ?: error("missing")
        if (requested.compareAndSet(request, null)) tokenSuccess++
    }
    println("Float phase CAS success=$legacySuccess/100; request-token CAS success=$tokenSuccess/100")
    check(legacySuccess == 0)
    check(tokenSuccess == 100)
}
```

### Bounded correction required before another backend hypothesis

1. Replace AtomicReference<Float?> with an immutable **request identity object**, carrying monotonically increasing request id, expected phase, expected current lease and per-request completion/result. Retain the exact request object read by onProduced for CAS. Phase tolerance is for numerical frame matching only. Do not replace this with getAndSet(null), a boxed Double, a blind set(null) or a larger timeout: those either retain the identity bug or let a late A clear B.
